mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior month's level coincides with a decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its previous month's value by more than 0.25 percentage points within the same month.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period, 20-day forward returns do not show statistically significant negative excess returns (t-test p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS up moves of >0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a concurrent rise in S&P 500 60-day forward returns signals a labor market softening that reduces growth expectations and dampens equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds the prior month's value by at least 10,000 and persists for two consecutive months.
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market weakening
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically lower than the 6-month pre-signaling mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds the prior month by more than 0.3 percentage points, S&P 500 20-day forward returns turn positive as investors anticipate future rate cuts.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following such inflation spikes, forward returns are not statistically higher than the 20-day average of the prior 10 windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening economic momentum and reduced corporate optimism.
failure_condition: During such INDPRO contractions, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the mean of the prior 8 such events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below the 50th percentile of its 12-month history, S&P 500 60-day forward returns trend positive as expectations of future easing rise.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS < median(FEDFUNDS, 12 months).
regime_hint: Shift to accommodative monetary policy regime
failure_condition: Over 60 days following such a signal, 60-day forward returns do not show statistically significant positive excess returns (t-test p > 0.05) versus the 60-day pre-signal window mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months coincides with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as labor market tightness supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.0% for two consecutive months.
failure_condition: During such periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 20-day average of the prior 5 such labor market tightness windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (not available in catalog) are replaced by a proxy: simultaneous increases in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales index) above their prior month's levels jointly predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via dual demand signals.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST and RSAFS month-over-month changes are each greater than +5%.
failure_condition: During such joint signals, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of the prior 4 joint double-signal events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in building permits (not available in catalog) replaced by: when HOUST (housing starts) falls by more than 15% month-over-month, S&P 500 20-day forward returns turn negative due to supply-side weakness and reduced investment optimism.
failure_condition: During such events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the mean of the prior 3 single-supply-downturn windows (t-test p > 0.05).
